findings.title: Aperture, judgment, and disclosure
findings.claim: The demanded al-fatḥ can carry an aperture, a water outlet, and a verdict. The irrigation scene in 32:27 makes release through an opening newly visible; the answer in 32:29 places the event at a day when late belief brings no benefit or extension. The truth condition also leaves a confirmation reading live, while the answer's consequence for those who disbelieve gives the event a contestive edge.
findings.mechanism: In the focus, the definite event noun ٱلْفَتْحُ is asked about by مَتَىٰ and placed under the condition إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ. In 32:27, water is driven toward barren ground, growth emerges, and provision follows; that separate process activates the physical-opening and outlet-water facets. The response in 32:29 names the day of the opening, denies benefit and respite, and identifies those who disbelieve; these details activate judgment, disclosure, and a bounded victory reading while answering the truth challenge. The same answer supports a future expectation without depicting its realization as already complete.
findings.reader_payoff: The question's object becomes more than an event label: it can be pictured as release through an opening and as a disclosed, decisive outcome whose effects cannot be changed by a late response.
findings.containment: The plain question about when remains intact. The water scene is an analogy supplied by the pericope, not a claim that 32:28 describes irrigation. Judgment and victory can coexist, and the answer asserts a future consequence rather than narrating the event as already enacted.
